samples.summary: 'wires every namespace' test uses arrayContaining and omits the `files` namespace
samples.evidence: buildProgram() in src/cli.ts registers 11 namespaces including registerFilesCommand (files.ts:13 `.command('files')`), but the assertion at output.test.ts:370-383 lists only 10 names and uses `expect.arrayContaining`, so dropping `registerFilesCommand(program)` from buildProgram would leave this test green despite the test name claiming 'every namespace'. A `toEqual`/`expect.arrayContaining` with all 11 (or a set comparison) would actually pin the wiring.

samples.summary: --quiet regression guards only cover docs/sheets; the other 5 namespaces whose call sites changed are unguarded
samples.evidence: The diff removes the `quiet` argument from output/outputError at call sites in api-keys.ts, files.ts, notes.ts, slides.ts, tabs.ts, schema.ts, sheets-import/export.ts. The regression describe's local buildProgram (output.test.ts:233-238) registers only docs and sheets, so reintroducing quiet-suppression in e.g. notes.ts or files.ts would not fail any test — contradicting the comment at line 174-180 claiming 'Reintroducing suppression at any of these call sites fails these tests'. Grep of packages/cli/test for 'quiet' shows no other command-level quiet-body test.

samples.summary: stdin branch of `sheets cells batch` moved inside the try but only the --data branch is tested
samples.evidence: cells.ts now wraps both the `--data` JSON.parse and the stdin read+parse in the try so failures reach the envelope. output.test.ts:284 only covers `--data '{'`; no test feeds malformed/failing stdin (no `process.stdin` stub anywhere in packages/cli/test per grep). The stdin path's envelope behavior is therefore asserted only by comment.

samples.summary: bin.test.ts mocks the entire cli module and asserts only that a mock was called
samples.evidence: vi.mock('../src/cli.js') replaces both runCli and buildProgram, so the test can only observe `runCli` being invoked with no arguments (lines 17-20). It proves the one-line delegation and nothing about program construction or the error envelope; acceptable for a shebang entrypoint, but it is pure mock-call coverage and should not be read as covering runCli behavior.
